headline: Hungarian Farmers May Also Suffer as China Floods the World with Subsidy-Fattened Meat
summary: China's meat and dairy overproduction is growing, aided in part by state subsidies, and Chinese companies are turning to foreign markets with cheap products, a trend seen earlier in solar panels, batteries and EVs.
why: China is a major global food producer and importer, so surpluses from its subsidised farming can shift export prices and competition in agricultural markets worldwide.
